title: Centralize and triage enterprise compliance requests (playbook + SLAs)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise prospects and customers submit diverse compliance requests (SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA attestation, GDPR/DPA clauses, and vendor questionnaires) through Sales, Support, and Security teams. Requests are currently routed ad-hoc, causing slow response times, duplicated effort across teams, and inconsistent artifacts (DPA templates, questionnaire answers, evidence bundles).

Goal: Create a centralized playbook and operational flow that standardizes intake, triage, prioritization, and response for enterprise security & compliance requests. Deliverables: 1) standardized intake form and routing rules; 2) triage rubric with SLAs and priority mapping; 3) canonical response templates (DPA, high-level SOC2 summary, common questionnaire answers); 4) owner matrix (Security, Legal, PM, Sales/CS roles); 5) automation plan to reduce manual handoffs (Zendesk/HubSpot -> Linear flow or a lightweight internal queue); 6) training and handoff docs for AEs/CS/Support.

Success metrics: median time-to-first-response under 48 hours for 'high' requests, 80% of frequently asked questionnaire items covered by canonical templates, reduction in duplicate evidence creation by 60%, and a documented single source-of-truth for evidence bundles.

Scope: Non-bug intake & triage process work only (no engineering changes to runtime or infra); however, dependencies with ENG and Security will be tracked for automation and any tooling requests. This plays on Redwood's positioning to reduce friction for enterprise procurement while protecting product and legal risks.
